remainingGaps.intent: Family subscription purchase entitlement versus shared calendar data
remainingGaps.evidence: Subscription guide separates Apple billing identity from provider/sharing identity, but does not establish whether a particular purchase is eligible for family entitlement sharing. Whole-calendar guide explains invitations but not this common purchase/access ambiguity.
remainingGaps.recommendation: Add one bounded FAQ to the existing whole-calendar or subscription guide only after checking current Apple entitlement guidance and the actual product eligibility. Explain that calendar access is separately granted; do not claim Cloud subscriptions are or are not Family Sharing eligible from these bodies.

strongestExistingGuideImprovement.action: Clarify selected-calendar side effects, then add a brief restore-and-review step within the existing colour/visibility section.

exactChanges.before: Give work and personal calendars distinct colours, then check a busy day with both visible. When you want a narrower view, hide a calendar rather than deleting its events. Apple’s duplicate-calendar guide explains how to show and hide calendars with checkboxes.
exactChanges.after: Give work and personal calendars distinct colours, then check a busy day with both visible. When you want a narrower view, hide a calendar rather than deleting its events. Apple’s duplicate-calendar guide explains how to show and hide calendars with checkboxes. Before accepting a new commitment, restore the calendars relevant to that decision and compare the week with all of them visible. An empty filtered view does not establish that the time is free.

exactChanges.before: Hiding is a display choice. It is not a change to who can access the calendar, and you should check notification settings separately if the goal is a quiet evening. Keep an approved work app available if your organisation requires it.
exactChanges.after: Hiding a calendar does not change who has permission to access it. In Cloud Calendars, calendar selection also matters to Google synchronization and notification scheduling, so do not assume that deselecting a calendar affects only the picture on screen. Check important changes at their provider and review notification settings separately if the goal is a quiet evening. Keep an approved work app available if your organisation requires it.
